# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 exporting manufacturers). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| supplier_diversity | Number of distinct input suppliers (standardized), 2021-2022 |
| export_growth_2023 | Export value growth in 2023 (percent index) |
| log_sales_2020 | Log sales, 2020 |
| years_exporting_2020 | Years since first export, standardized, 2020 |
| export_growth_2020 | Export value growth in 2020, standardized |
| buyer_rating_2023 | Average rating from foreign buyers, 2023 |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| product_group | Sector: durables / nondurables |
| inventory_days_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_imported_inputs_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| port_distance_km | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| certified_iso | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| debt_ratio_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Effect of supplier diversification on export growth

**Conclusion: positive effect (modest).** Preferred estimate: +0.693 export-growth index points per 1 SD of supplier_diversity, HC1 SE 0.240, p = 0.0038 (95% CI 0.22 to 1.16). The mean of the outcome is about 100.5.

Preferred specification: OLS of export_growth_2023 on supplier_diversity plus all pre-period controls: log sales, years exporting, 2020 export growth, inventory days, foreign ownership, imported-input share, port distance, ISO certification, debt ratio, listed, region and product group. Standard errors are HC1 robust, N = 2000.

## Why this specification
The naive estimate is confounded: larger, more experienced firms have more suppliers and also grow faster. Adjusting for pre-period covariates cuts the estimate to about a quarter of the naive value. The estimate is identical across the adjusted specifications that exclude buyer_rating_2023 (0.69). buyer_rating_2023 is measured in 2023, the same period as the outcome. It correlates 0.54 with supplier diversity, so it is probably affected by diversity and is a post-treatment variable. Controlling for it would bias the estimate, so I excluded it. Including it flips the sign, which I judge to be a bad-control artifact.

The data are a cross-section, so the effect is identified only under selection on observables. Unmeasured confounding is possible, and the estimate should be read as an adjusted association with a causal interpretation conditional on that assumption.

## All specifications estimated (5)
| # | Specification | Coef | SE (HC1) | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Naive: diversity only | 2.553 | 0.246 | 3e-25 |
| 2 | **Preferred: + all pre-period controls, region, product group** | **0.693** | **0.240** | **0.0038** |
| 3 | Preferred controls + buyer_rating_2023 (bad control, not preferred) | -2.121 | 0.233 | 8e-20 |
| 4 | Basic controls: log sales, years exporting, 2020 export growth | 0.691 | 0.240 | 0.0040 |
| 5 | Preferred controls + squared diversity term (linear coef shown) | 0.694 | 0.240 | 0.0038 |

content.text:
I approved the report and wrote `verdict.json`.

I re-ran the preferred specification and got the same result: +0.693 per 1 SD of supplier diversity, with an HC1 standard error of 0.240.

- **Excluding the 2023 buyer rating:** I think this is the right call. The rating is measured in the same period as the outcome and correlates 0.54 with supplier diversity. Adding it flips the estimate to −2.121, which fits the report's bad-control explanation.
- **Stability:** The controlled estimate barely moves when the control set changes (0.693 with all pre-period controls, 0.691 with only sales, years exporting and 2020 export growth). The drop from the naive 2.553 is mostly firm size and experience.
- **Causal caveat:** The report states that this is a cross-section identified only under selection on observables. It calls the effect modest and does not overclaim.

I did not independently re-check the squared-term specification. I also did not test for remaining unmeasured confounding beyond what the report already flags.
